transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Hi. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I guess I came in because... well, I hope I'm explaining this okay, but I just can't stop feeling like everything that goes wrong lately is entirely my fault. 

I've been feeling like such a bad employee, and... and a bad homeowner, too. It’s just this heavy feeling that I somehow deserve to lose what I’ve worked so hard for. I know that probably sounds awful, and I'm really sorry if it seems like I'm just overreacting to things, but... does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um... well, I always try to just push through it, you know, so I don't let anyone down at work. But... I guess it's been going on for a while now. It's been about two years and one month, I think? That's when I really started noticing the... the sadness, and just losing interest in things. 

I know I probably should have come in sooner, and I'm really sorry I waited so long to get help. I just didn't want to make a fuss or be a bother to anyone. Is... is that specific enough? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need for your notes.
During these two years, have you had any period lasting at least two months when you felt essentially back to your usual self?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I really try to be my usual self, I really do. But... looking back, the low mood and the, um, just not caring about things... it's pretty much been there almost the whole time since this all started. 

There were maybe a few brief periods where I could function a little better, where I could force a smile and get through the workday without everyone noticing. But it never really lasted for two whole months. I'm sorry, I wish I could give you a better answer, like I had bounced back more. Does that make sense, though? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Have you noticed any change in your sleep during this period?

Um... well, my sleep has been a little off, I guess. I mean, I still get *some* rest, so it's not like I'm completely falling apart or anything! But... most nights, I end up just lying awake for hours. I try so hard to fall asleep, but I just end up listening to the house settle. 

And then, even when I do finally drift off, I usually wake up around three or four in the morning. And... I just can't seem to get back to sleep before I have to get up for work. I know I should be managing it better, maybe drinking less coffee or something, and I'm really sorry if that sounds like I'm just complaining about normal stress. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope that's helpful.
During these past two years, have you felt depressed or down for most of the day on most days?

Um... well, I guess so? I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm just feeling sorry for myself all the time. I really do try to put on a brave face, especially at work. I don't want my team to think I'm slacking off or bringing everyone down. 

But... if I'm being completely honest, yeah. Most days, for most of the day, there's just this heavy, down feeling that I can't seem to shake off. Even when I'm smiling in a meeting, it's kind of just sitting there in the background. I really wish I could just snap out of it, and I'm sorry I haven't been able to. Does... does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
During this period, have you often felt low in energy or unusually tired?

Um... well, not really? I mean, I definitely get a little tired sometimes, but who doesn't, right? Working in operations, things get pretty busy, so it's totally normal to feel a bit drained by the end of the day. I really try to push through it and stay on top of my projects. 

I wouldn't say I'm unusually tired or anything like that. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around doing nothing. I still manage to get my work done, even if I need an extra cup of coffee. So, um, no, I don't think I've felt super low in energy. Is that... is that okay? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
During this period, have you often felt that you were inadequate or had very low self-esteem?

Um... well... I guess I do struggle with that sometimes. I mean, I know I shouldn't be so hard on myself, and I really try to stay positive! But... it's just that lately, I can't stop feeling like everything that goes wrong is somehow my fault. 

Like... if a project at work hits a snag, even if it's out of my hands, I just feel like I'm a terrible employee. And then I come home, and if the house is a mess or something breaks, I just feel like a bad homeowner. It's like... I almost feel like I deserve to lose everything I've worked so hard for. Which I know sounds awful, and I'm really sorry if that sounds dramatic! I know I should be more grateful for what I have. But that's actually a big part of why I came in... I just can't seem to shake this feeling that I'm just... inadequate. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
During these past two years, have you often felt hopeless about the future?

Um... well, no, not really. I mean, I always try to look on the bright side of things, you know? I really believe that if you just work hard and keep a positive attitude, things will work out eventually. 

I know I've been feeling down lately, but I don't think it means my whole future is ruined or anything. I still have goals at work and things I want to accomplish. I definitely don't want to sound like I've just given up, because I haven't! I'm still trying my best every day. So, um, no, I wouldn't say I feel hopeless. Is... is that a good thing? I hope that's what you were looking for.
During this period, have you often had trouble concentrating or making decisions?

Um... no, I don't think I've had any real trouble with that. Working in operations, I kind of have to be on the ball with decisions all day, you know? So I really push myself to stay super focused. 

I mean, sure, sometimes I might take a little extra time to double-check a spreadsheet before I send it off, just to be absolutely sure it's right... but I don't think that means I can't concentrate. I'm still getting all my tasks done on time! I definitely wouldn't say I'm struggling to focus or anything like that. I really try to stay sharp. 

Is... is that the kind of answer you need? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and giving you the right details.
During this period, have you noticed any change in your appetite?

Um... well... I guess my appetite has been a little bit unpredictable lately. I mean, I really try to make sure I'm eating, but sometimes I get so busy at work that I just sort of... forget to have a proper lunch. 

I don't want it to sound like I'm starving myself or anything like that! It's just that during the day, I mostly end up skipping real meals. Then I'll just grab some coffee or a piece of toast—you know, whatever is easiest and quickest. I did notice the other day that my clothes are fitting a little looser than usual, which... I guess means I've lost some weight. But I promise I'm not doing it on purpose! I know I need to do a better job of taking care of myself and eating regular meals. I'm going to try harder to pack a lunch, I really am. 

Does... does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I haven't been eating as well as I should be.
During this period, have you often lost interest in or stopped enjoying activities that you usually enjoy?

Um... well... I guess I'd have to say I'm still doing a lot of the things I usually do. I really try to keep my weekends busy! 

I used to love planning brunches with my friends, and I'd spend hours painting in the spare room, or... or I'd go hiking, and I even signed up for all these professional networking events. And I still do those things, I really do! It's just... lately, I guess they feel a little bit more like... like tasks on a to-do list? Like I'm just sort of going through the motions and pretending to care about them as much as I used to. 

But I haven't stopped doing them! I know it's important to stay active and keep up with friends, so I really push myself to keep going. I don't want to be someone who just sits at home all weekend, you know? So I'm still trying my best to be involved and do the things I'm supposed to do. 

Is... is that the right way to look at it? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm being lazy or ungrateful for my friends.
Since these symptoms began, have you had any period of several weeks when you felt completely free of depressed mood and loss of interest?

Um... well... there actually was a time, maybe for a few weeks, where things felt a little... lighter? Like, my mood wasn't quite as heavy, and I was getting through my work days a lot more normally. I was really proud of how well I was handling everything at the office! 

But... um... I guess I should mention, even though I was feeling better, I... I still heard that voice over by the air vents sometimes. And I still felt pretty sure that the mortgage company and some of my coworkers were keeping tabs on me. I really tried to ignore it and just focus on being productive, I promise! I didn't let it stop me from doing my job. 

Does... does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I still had those... those other things going on, even when I wasn't feeling as down. I really was trying my best to stay positive!

Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt neither depressed nor uninterested in things, but still heard the voice or believed that the mortgage company or coworkers were monitoring you?

Um... yes, I think... I think that's exactly what I was just trying to say. I'm sorry if I wasn't clear before! 

There was that stretch, like I mentioned, for a few weeks where my mood really did feel a lot better. I wasn't feeling so down, and I was getting through my work days, you know, normally. I was really trying to be a good employee and stay on top of my projects. 

But... yeah, even during that time when I wasn't feeling depressed, I... I still heard that voice near the air vents. And I still felt pretty convinced that the mortgage company and my coworkers were keeping tabs on me. I really tried to just push through it and not let it bother anyone else, though! I didn't want to make a fuss or seem crazy. 

Is... is it normal to still have those things happen even when you aren't feeling sad? I really hope I'm explaining this right... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.

opening_question.intent: Establish the patient's main reason for seeking care
opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: Persistent depressive symptoms for over two years with auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions that continued during a period of at least two weeks without depressed mood or loss of interest, supporting schizoaffective disorder, depressive type.

confirmed_symptoms: Depressed mood for most of the day on most days
Markedly reduced enjoyment or emotional engagement in previously pleasurable activities
Insomnia with prolonged sleep onset and early-morning awakening
Reduced appetite with unintentional weight loss
Feelings of inadequacy, excessive self-blame, and low self-esteem
Auditory hallucination described as hearing a voice near the air vents
Persecutory delusional belief that the mortgage company and coworkers were monitoring or keeping tabs on the patient
Auditory hallucinations and persecutory beliefs persisted during a period of at least two weeks when depressed mood and loss of interest were absent

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Depressive symptoms have been present for approximately two years and one month without a symptom-free period lasting two months; psychotic symptoms persisted during several weeks of improved mood, including at least two weeks without depression or anhedonia.
additional_requirements: Psychotic symptoms occurring for at least two weeks in the absence of prominent mood symptoms was explicitly verified
No sustained two-month return to usual functioning during the depressive course was reported
